literal: Posthumously he was granted command over military affairs in the three provinces of Jing, Qi, and Bin; his rank was advanced to Duke; his posthumous title was Minzhuang.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted command over military affairs in the three provinces of Jing, Qi, and Bin; his rank was advanced to duke; his posthumous title was Minzhuang.

literal: The Grand Ancestor grieved for him, came in person to mourn, and granted his wife and children stipends as though Xingjing were still alive.
idiomatic: Gao Huan grieved for him, came in person to mourn, and granted his wife and children stipends as though Xingjing were still alive.

literal: His son Shilin succeeded.
idiomatic: His son Shilin succeeded.

literal: Wang Huai, styled Huaizhou, was a man whose origins are unknown.
idiomatic: Wang Huai, styled Huaizhou, was a man whose origins are unknown.

literal: From youth he loved bow and horse and possessed considerable martial spirit; when the northern frontier fell into turmoil, he entered military service early.
idiomatic: From youth he loved bow and horse and possessed considerable martial spirit; when the northern frontier fell into turmoil, he entered military service early.

literal: When Han Lou rebelled in You Province, Huai knew he would not succeed; he secretly rallied his intimates, and at the beginning of Zhongxing rebelled against Lou and returned to Wei, receiving appointment as General Who Subdues Captives, first chief of a dependent people, and Marquis of Wuzhou County.
idiomatic: When Han Lou rebelled in You Province, Wang Huai knew he would not succeed; he secretly rallied his intimates, and at the beginning of Zhongxing rebelled against Lou and returned to Wei, receiving appointment as general who subdues captives, first chief of a dependent people, and marquis of Wuzhou County.

literal: When the Grand Ancestor marched east, Huai led more than three thousand households of his followers and joined him in Ji Province.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan marched east, Wang Huai led more than three thousand households of his followers and joined him in Ji Province.

literal: When the banner of righteousness was raised, the Grand Ancestor made him Grand Commander; he followed in the campaign against Erzhu Zhao at Guang'a, defeated him, and was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Yu Province.
idiomatic: When the banner of righteousness was raised, Gao Huan made him grand commander; he followed in the campaign against Erzhu Zhao at Guang'a, defeated him, and was appointed general who pacifies the north and governor of Yu Province.

literal: He again followed the Grand Ancestor in assaulting Ye, captured it, and followed in defeating the Four Huns at Hanling; his rank was advanced to Marquis.
idiomatic: He again followed Gao Huan in assaulting Ye, captured it, and followed in defeating the Four Huns at Hanling; his rank was advanced to marquis.

literal: He still followed him into Luoyang, was appointed Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, and his enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Luxiang County.
idiomatic: He still followed Gao Huan into Luoyang, was appointed grand general of chariots and cavalry, and his enfeoffment was changed to marquis of Luxiang County.

literal: During Tianping he was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority with authority over military affairs in Guang Province.
idiomatic: During Tianping he was appointed bearer of the staff of authority with authority over military affairs in Guang Province.

literal: Liang sent generals Zhan Sengzhen and Yang Yan to raid; Huai together with mobile-circuit commissioner Yuan Yan attacked Xiangcheng, took it, and captured Yan.
idiomatic: Liang sent generals Zhan Sengzhen and Yang Yan to raid; Wang Huai together with mobile-circuit commissioner Yuan Yan attacked Xiangcheng, took it, and captured Yan.

literal: He again followed the Grand Ancestor in a surprise attack that captured Western Xia Province.
idiomatic: He again followed Gao Huan in a surprise attack that captured Western Xia Province.

literal: On returning, he became Grand Commander, garrisoned Xia Guan, and was appointed Commissioner with Protocol Equal to Three Imperators.
idiomatic: On returning, he became grand commander, garrisoned Xia Guan, and was appointed commissioner with protocol equal to three imperators.

literal: At the beginning of Yuanxiang, he became Grand Commander and campaigned west with the various generals; he fell ill and died at Jian Province.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanxiang, he became grand commander and campaigned west with the various generals; he fell ill and died at Jian Province.

literal: Posthumously he was granted authority over military affairs in the four provinces of Ding, You, Heng, and Si, plus governorship, Grand Steward, and Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted authority over military affairs in the four provinces of Ding, You, Heng, and Si, plus governorship, grand steward, and vice director of the masters of writing.

literal: Huai was known to the Grand Ancestor for his martial skill and loyal service; his ambitions were never fully realized, and commentators lamented that he did not fulfill his promise.
idiomatic: Wang Huai was known to Gao Huan for his martial skill and loyal service; his ambitions were never fully realized, and commentators lamented that he did not fulfill his promise.

literal: At the beginning of Huangjian, he was granted a place in offerings at the Grand Ancestor's temple court.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Huangjian, he was granted a place in offerings at Gao Huan's temple court.

literal: Liu Gui was a native of Yangqu in Xiurong.
idiomatic: Liu Gui was a native of Yangqu in Xiurong.

literal: His father Gan was posthumously granted Front General and Governor of Si Province during Wei.
idiomatic: His father Gan was posthumously granted front general and governor of Si Province during Wei.

literal: Gui was stern of character and decisive; he served successively as cavalry adjutant in Erzhu Rong's headquarters.
idiomatic: Liu Gui was stern of character and decisive; he served successively as cavalry adjutant in Erzhu Rong's headquarters.

literal: At the beginning of Jianyi, for his part in planning and merit, he was enfeoffed Baron of Fucheng County with a fief of five hundred households.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianyi, for his part in planning and merit, he was enfeoffed baron of Fucheng County with a fief of five hundred households.

literal: He was appointed Left General and Grand Master for Consultation, and soon was advanced to Duke.
idiomatic: He was appointed left general and grand master for consultation, and soon was advanced to duke.

literal: Rong's nature was fierce and impatient; Gui was especially stern and rigorous; whenever entrusted with a task he mostly satisfied Rong's wishes, and so won trust and favor — his status and reputation grew daily, and he was additionally made General Who Pacifies the Army.
idiomatic: Erzhu Rong's nature was fierce and impatient; Liu Gui was especially stern and rigorous; whenever entrusted with a task he mostly satisfied Rong's wishes, and so won trust and favor — his status and reputation grew daily, and he was additionally made general who pacifies the army.

literal: In the third year of Yongan, he was appointed Governor of Liang Province.
idiomatic: In the third year of Yongan, he was appointed governor of Liang Province.

literal: At the beginning of Jianming, Erzhu Shilong held sole power and made Gui General Who Campaigns in the South, Bearer of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, concurrently Left Vice Director, and Commissioner of the Western Circuit, to oppose Emperor Xiaozhuang's mobile-circuit commissioner Yuan Xiangong at Zhengping.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianming, Erzhu Shilong held sole power and made Liu Gui general who campaigns in the south, bearer of the golden seal and purple ribbon, concurrently left vice director, and commissioner of the western circuit, to oppose Emperor Xiaozhuang's mobile-circuit commissioner Yuan Xiangong at Zhengping.

literal: Gui defeated Xiangong, captured him together with Grand Commander Pei Jun and others, and was again appointed Governor of Jin Province.
idiomatic: Liu Gui defeated Xiangong, captured him together with grand commander Pei Jun and others, and was again appointed governor of Jin Province.

literal: At the beginning of Putai, he was transferred to administer Bing Province affairs.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Putai, he was transferred to administer Bing Province affairs.

literal: When the Grand Ancestor raised righteousness, Gui abandoned his city and joined him at Ye.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan raised righteousness, Liu Gui abandoned his city and joined him at Ye.

literal: At the beginning of Taichang, he was appointed Governor of Si Province in his existing rank and transferred to administer Jian Province affairs.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Taichang, he was appointed governor of Si Province in his existing rank and transferred to administer Jian Province affairs.

literal: At the beginning of Tianping, he was appointed Governor of Shan Province.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianping, he was appointed governor of Shan Province.

literal: In the fourth year, he was appointed Censor-in-Chief and Chief Arbiter of Si Province.
idiomatic: In the fourth year, he was appointed censor-in-chief and chief arbiter of Si Province.

literal: That same year, he was additionally made Mobile-Circuit Vice Director and, together with Hou Jing, Gao Ang, and others, campaigned against Dugu Ruyuan at Luoyang.
idiomatic: That same year, he was additionally made mobile-circuit vice director and, together with Hou Jing, Gao Ang, and others, campaigned against Dugu Ruyuan at Luoyang.

literal: Ren Yanjing was a native of Guangning.
idiomatic: Ren Yanjing was a native of Guangning.

literal: His uncle's elder brother Tao, at the beginning of Taihe, served as General of the Army at Yunzhong; Yanjing followed him and there established his household.
idiomatic: His uncle's elder brother Tao, at the beginning of Taihe, served as general of the army at Yunzhong; Ren Yanjing followed him and there established his household.

literal: Yanjing from youth was mild and generous, with breadth of character.
idiomatic: Ren Yanjing from youth was mild and generous, with breadth of character.

literal: He initially followed Ge Rong as a bandit; Rong appointed him king and greatly entrusted him.
idiomatic: He initially followed Ge Rong as a bandit; Ge Rong appointed him king and greatly entrusted him.

literal: When Rong was defeated, Yanjing led his own troops in surrendering first and was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distant, Governor of Guangning, and enfeoffed Duke of Xihe County.
idiomatic: When Ge Rong was defeated, Ren Yanjing led his own troops in surrendering first and was appointed general who pacifies the distant, governor of Guangning, and enfeoffed duke of Xihe County.

literal: Later he followed the Grand Ancestor in raising righteousness; at the beginning of Zhongxing he was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
idiomatic: Later he followed Gao Huan in raising righteousness; at the beginning of Zhongxing he was repeatedly promoted to grand master of splendid happiness.

literal: At the beginning of Taichang, he was repeatedly transferred to Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and advanced to Commissioner of the First Rank with Protocol Equal to Three Imperators.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Taichang, he was repeatedly transferred to left vice director of the masters of writing and advanced to commissioner of the first rank with protocol equal to three imperators.

literal: Yanjing's rank and reputation were already weighty, and he could treat others with forbearance and kindness — gentry and commoners alike praised him.
idiomatic: Ren Yanjing's rank and reputation were already weighty, and he could treat others with forbearance and kindness — gentry and commoners alike praised him.

literal: When Husi Chun's treachery broke out, Yanjing abandoned his household and fled north to Hebei Commandery, where he rallied the local people and held it, awaiting the Grand Ancestor.
idiomatic: When Husi Chun's treachery broke out, Ren Yanjing abandoned his household and fled north to Hebei Commandery, where he rallied the local people and held it, awaiting Gao Huan.

literal: When Emperor Wu of Wei entered the Pass, the Jing barbarians were rebellious; Yanjing was appointed Bearer of the Staff with the title Grand Commander of the Southern Circuit and pacified them.
idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Wei entered the Pass, the Jing barbarians were rebellious; Ren Yanjing was appointed bearer of the staff with the title grand commander of the southern circuit and pacified them.

literal: At the beginning of Tianping, he was again appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianping, he was again appointed attendant-in-ordinary.

literal: At that time Lu Zhongyan of Fanyang led displaced people of Hebei in rebellion at Yangxia, and Tian Long of Western Yan Province gathered a host in response; Yanjing was made Grand Commander and Military Coordinator of the Eastern Circuit and led Grand Commanders Yuan Zheng, Chilie Tuo, and others to suppress them.
idiomatic: At that time Lu Zhongyan of Fanyang led displaced people of Hebei in rebellion at Yangxia, and Tian Long of Western Yan Province gathered a host in response; Ren Yanjing was made grand commander and military coordinator of the eastern circuit and led grand commanders Yuan Zheng, Chilie Tuo, and others to suppress them.

literal: Soon he became Mobile-Circuit Vice Director and was appointed Governor of Xu Province.
idiomatic: Soon he became mobile-circuit vice director and was appointed governor of Xu Province.

literal: At that time Liang sent Yuan Qinghe and his generals to raid the frontier; Yanjing defeated Liang's Governor of Ren Province Huang Daoshi at Northern Jiyin and defeated Liang Jun at Shanfu, capturing and slaying ten thousand men.
idiomatic: At that time Liang sent Yuan Qinghe and his generals to raid the frontier; Ren Yanjing defeated Liang's governor of Ren Province Huang Daoshi at Northern Jiyin and defeated Liang Jun at Shanfu, capturing and slaying ten thousand men.

literal: He was again appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary.
idiomatic: He was again appointed attendant-in-ordinary.

literal: While administering the province he accepted large bribes.
idiomatic: While administering the province he accepted large bribes.

literal: Yet his governance was not cruel; he treated gentry with courtesy and respect, and the people did not suffer greatly under him.
idiomatic: Yet his governance was not cruel; he treated gentry with courtesy and respect, and the people did not suffer greatly under him.

literal: He Ruo Hui, chief clerk of Ying Province, seized Governor Tian Xun, held the city, and surrendered to Western Wei; Yanjing was again ordered to lead Yuzhou Governor Yao Xiong and others against them.
idiomatic: He Ruo Hui, chief clerk of Ying Province, seized Governor Tian Xun, held the city, and surrendered to Western Wei; Ren Yanjing was again ordered to lead Yuzhou Governor Yao Xiong and others against them.

literal: Western Wei sent its general Yi Feng with troops to the rescue; Yanjing and the others were defeated in battle, withdrew to Northern Yu Province, then joined mobile-circuit commissioner Hou Jing, Grand Steward Gao Ang, and others, jointly attacked Yingchuan, and took it.
idiomatic: Western Wei sent its general Yi Feng with troops to the rescue; Ren Yanjing and the others were defeated in battle, withdrew to Northern Yu Province, then joined mobile-circuit commissioner Hou Jing, grand steward Gao Ang, and others, jointly attacked Yingchuan, and took it.

literal: In the autumn of the first year of Yuanxiang he died at Ye; he was forty-five.
idiomatic: In the autumn of the first year of Yuanxiang he died at Ye; he was forty-five.

literal: Posthumously he was granted Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Grand Guardian, Grand Commandant, Overseer of Masters-of-Writing Affairs, and authority over military affairs in the five provinces of Ji, Ding, Ying, You, and An, plus governorship of Ji Province.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted bearer of the staff of authority, grand guardian, grand commandant, overseer of masters-of-writing affairs, and authority over military affairs in the five provinces of Ji, Ding, Ying, You, and An, plus governorship of Ji Province.

literal: His son Zhou succeeded.
idiomatic: His son Zhou succeeded.

literal: Zhou was dashing and chivalric, and fairly quick-witted.
idiomatic: Zhou was dashing and chivalric, and fairly quick-witted.

literal: From youth he was at the Grand Ancestor's side; in the Tianping era he was promoted to Governor of Dong Commandery.
idiomatic: From youth he was at Gao Huan's side; in the Tianping era he was promoted to governor of Dong Commandery.

literal: His household was already wealthy, and he also amassed riches; his manner was extremely extravagant, and guests who came and went were received with the greatest hospitality.
idiomatic: His household was already wealthy, and he also amassed riches; his manner was extremely extravagant, and guests who came and went were received with the greatest hospitality.

literal: Soon he was impeached for graft by the relevant offices, but the Grand Ancestor pardoned him.
idiomatic: Soon he was impeached for graft by the relevant offices, but Gao Huan pardoned him.

literal: When he left his commandery post, the Grand Ancestor made him a Grand Commander.
idiomatic: When he left his commandery post, Gao Huan made him a grand commander.

literal: At the end of Xinghe, when the Grand Ancestor returned from attacking Yubi, because southwestern Jin Province was strategically vital he left Duke of Qinghe Yue as mobile-circuit commissioner to garrison it, and Zhou was placed under his command.
idiomatic: At the end of Xinghe, when Gao Huan returned from attacking Yubi, because southwestern Jin Province was strategically vital he left Duke of Qinghe Yue as mobile-circuit commissioner to garrison it, and Zhou was placed under his command.

literal: Zhou drank and roamed at leisure, failing to keep vigilant guard; the Grand Ancestor reprimanded him.
idiomatic: Zhou drank and roamed at leisure, failing to keep vigilant guard; Gao Huan reprimanded him.

literal: Zhou was afraid and secretly sent envoys to offer submission to Zhou.
idiomatic: Zhou was afraid and secretly sent envoys to offer submission to Northern Zhou.

literal: Someone reported and denounced him; though investigation pursued to the end no proof was found, and the Grand Ancestor specially pardoned him, saying to Zhou: "I extend sincerity toward all things and believed you could surely have no such design.
idiomatic: Someone reported and denounced him; though investigation pursued to the end no proof was found, and Gao Huan specially pardoned him, saying to Zhou: "I extend sincerity toward all things and believed you could surely have no such design.

literal: Moreover, Yuwen Tai's surrendered men come one after another — whether your conduct is true or false, why fear it will not be known afterward.
idiomatic: Moreover, Yuwen Tai's surrendered men come one after another — whether your conduct is true or false, why fear it will not be known afterward.

literal: " Zhou inwardly could not rest at ease.
idiomatic: " Zhou inwardly could not rest at ease.

literal: At that time Commissioner with Protocol Equal to Three Imperators Erzhu Wenchang, adjutants Fang Ziyuan, Zheng Zhongli, and others were all treacherous, base, and worthless; Zhou cultivated close ties with them and secretly plotted regicide.
idiomatic: At that time commissioner with protocol equal to three imperators Erzhu Wenchang, adjutants Fang Ziyuan, Zheng Zhongli, and others were all treacherous, base, and worthless; Zhou cultivated close ties with them and secretly plotted regicide.

literal: On the fifteenth day of the first month in the third year of Wuding, taking advantage of the Grand Ancestor's nightly entertainments, they plotted to strike by surprise.
idiomatic: On the fifteenth day of the first month in the third year of Wuding, taking advantage of Gao Huan's nightly entertainments, they plotted to strike by surprise.

literal: Someone reported them; an order went out to arrest and investigate to the end, and everything was confirmed.
idiomatic: Someone reported them; an order went out to arrest and investigate to the end, and everything was confirmed.

literal: Zhou and his sons and younger brothers were all executed.
idiomatic: Zhou and his sons and younger brothers were all executed.

literal: Moduoluo Daiwen was a native of Dina in Tai'an.
idiomatic: Moduoluo Daiwen was a native of Dina in Tai'an.

literal: He was fierce and resolute, with courage and mettle.
idiomatic: He was fierce and resolute, with courage and mettle.

literal: He followed the Grand Ancestor in raising righteousness.
idiomatic: He followed Gao Huan in raising righteousness.

literal: At the beginning of Zhongxing, he was appointed General Who Calms the Waves, Gentlemen-at-Arms Central Palace Guard, and Grand Commander of the Guard Corps.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhongxing, he was appointed general who calms the waves, gentlemen-at-arms central palace guard, and grand commander of the guard corps.

literal: He followed the campaign against Erzhu Zhao at Guang'a, performed meritorious service, was additionally made Front General, and enfeoffed Viscount of Shicheng County with a fief of three hundred households.
idiomatic: He followed the campaign against Erzhu Zhao at Guang'a, performed meritorious service, was additionally made front general, and enfeoffed viscount of Shicheng County with a fief of three hundred households.

literal: He again followed in defeating the Four Huns at Hanling and his rank was advanced to Marquis.
idiomatic: He again followed in defeating the Four Huns at Hanling and his rank was advanced to marquis.

literal: He followed in pacifying Erzhu Zhao at Chihong Ridge.
idiomatic: He followed in pacifying Erzhu Zhao at Chihong Ridge.

literal: Zhao, driven to desperation, hanged himself; Daiwen recovered his corpse.
idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao, driven to desperation, hanged himself; Daiwen recovered his corpse.

literal: He was transferred to Grand Commander of the Left Wing.
idiomatic: He was transferred to grand commander of the left wing.

literal: When Husi Chun and others' treachery erupted, Emperor Wu of Wei sent Jia Xianzhi to hold and garrison Shiji.
idiomatic: When Husi Chun and others' treachery erupted, Emperor Wu of Wei sent Jia Xianzhi to hold and garrison Shiji.

literal: The Grand Ancestor ordered Daiwen to lead thirty thousand picked troops, join Dou Tai and others at Ding Province, march together on Shiji, and drive off Xianzhi.
idiomatic: Gao Huan ordered Daiwen to lead thirty thousand picked troops, join Dou Tai and others at Ding Province, march together on Shiji, and drive off Xianzhi.

literal: During Tianping he was appointed Governor of Jin Province.
idiomatic: During Tianping he was appointed governor of Jin Province.

literal: When Hu bandits of Bing Province raided and plundered, the Grand Ancestor personally campaigned against them, made Daiwen his vanguard, and he repeatedly won distinction in battle.
idiomatic: When Hu bandits of Bing Province raided and plundered, Gao Huan personally campaigned against them, made Daiwen his vanguard, and he repeatedly won distinction in battle.

literal: On returning, he was awarded thirty male and female servants, fifty head of cattle and horses each, and a thousand bolts of cloth, and was additionally made Grand Commander over the five provinces of Fen, Shan, Eastern Yong, Jin, and Tai.
idiomatic: On returning, he was awarded thirty male and female servants, fifty head of cattle and horses each, and a thousand bolts of cloth, and was additionally made grand commander over the five provinces of Fen, Shan, Eastern Yong, Jin, and Tai.

literal: Later he together with Grand Guardian Wei Jing attacked the two provinces of Eastern Yong and Southern Fen and captured them.
idiomatic: Later he together with grand guardian Wei Jing attacked the two provinces of Eastern Yong and Southern Fen and captured them.

literal: At the beginning of Yuanxiang, he was appointed Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Commissioner with Protocol Equal to Three Imperators, Grand Commander of the Southern Circuit, and together with mobile-circuit commissioner Hou Jing attacked Dugu Ruyuan at Jinyong City.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanxiang, he was appointed grand general of chariots and cavalry, commissioner with protocol equal to three imperators, grand commander of the southern circuit, and together with mobile-circuit commissioner Hou Jing attacked Dugu Ruyuan at Jinyong City.

literal: When Emperor Wen of Zhou's army came out through Hangu Pass, Jing and Gao Ang discussed marshaling the host and hardening the troops to await his arrival.
idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Zhou's army came out through Hangu Pass, Hou Jing and Gao Ang discussed marshaling the host and hardening the troops to await his arrival.

literal: Daiwen asked to lead his own troops to strike their vanguard, but Jing and the others firmly refused.
idiomatic: Daiwen asked to lead his own troops to strike their vanguard, but Hou Jing and the others firmly refused.

literal: Daiwen's nature was brave and willful; refusing to accept orders, he took a thousand light cavalry on forward reconnaissance, passed west beyond the Chan Stream, encountered Zhou troops, and fell in battle.
idiomatic: Daiwen's nature was brave and willful; refusing to accept orders, he took a thousand light cavalry on forward reconnaissance, passed west beyond the Chan Stream, encountered Zhou troops, and fell in battle.

literal: Posthumously he was granted military authority over the five provinces of Bing, Si, Heng, Yun, and Shuo, governorship of Bing Province, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Grand Steward.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted military authority over the five provinces of Bing, Si, Heng, Yun, and Shuo, governorship of Bing Province, right vice director of the masters of writing, and grand steward.

literal: His son Jingxian was upright, diligent, and capable; from youth he won notice for his martial prowess.
idiomatic: His son Jingxian was upright, diligent, and capable; from youth he won notice for his martial prowess.

literal: He constantly followed Hulü Guang on campaign and repeatedly won distinction.
idiomatic: He constantly followed Hulü Guang on campaign and repeatedly won distinction.

literal: Guang always ordered Jingxian to lead the van, set up camps and fortifications, and patrol at night — sometimes going until dawn without sleep.
idiomatic: Hulü Guang always ordered Jingxian to lead the van, set up camps and fortifications, and patrol at night — sometimes going until dawn without sleep.

literal: When facing the enemy and deploying battle arrays, he also had Jingxian assign ranks to officers and soldiers; in the blink of an eye the lines stood in perfect order.
idiomatic: When facing the enemy and deploying battle arrays, he also had Jingxian assign ranks to officers and soldiers; in the blink of an eye the lines stood in perfect order.

literal: Guang held him in deep esteem.
idiomatic: Hulü Guang held him in deep esteem.

literal: He rose to the rank of General of the Guards and was constantly charged with inspecting guard-corps affairs.
idiomatic: He rose to the rank of general of the guards and was constantly charged with inspecting guard-corps affairs.

literal: In the Wuping era, when the imperial carriage went to Jinyang, Jingxian was regularly ordered to supervise the capital's remaining troops and horses, investigate thieves and robbers — the capital grew solemn and orderly.
idiomatic: In the Wuping era, when the imperial carriage went to Jinyang, Jingxian was regularly ordered to supervise the capital's remaining troops and horses, investigate thieves and robbers — the capital grew solemn and orderly.

literal: In the seventh year, he followed the Late Emperor to Pingyang, was defeated and returned to Bing Province, and together with Tang Yong and others installed Prince of Ande and proclaimed him sovereign.
idiomatic: In the seventh year, he followed the Late Emperor to Pingyang, was defeated and returned to Bing Province, and together with Tang Yong and others installed Prince of Ande and proclaimed him sovereign.

literal: When Prince of Ande was defeated, civil and military officials all went over to the Zhou army — only Jingxian fled back to Ye.
idiomatic: When Prince of Ande was defeated, civil and military officials all went over to the Zhou army — only Jingxian fled back to Ye.

literal: He was appointed Grand Steward.
idiomatic: He was appointed grand steward.
